notes:
- A colour you kept is a colour you chose: "Retain anime colour" used to write one stored flag that did two different jobs: it kept the show's accent *and* it left the immersive layer switched on. So a retained title tinted every screen - the surfaces, the containers, the outlines - for as long as you left the switch alone, and the next launch found it still tinted. The opposite half was wrong too: a temporary colour waiting on its five-minute timer came back from a restart still applied, because the timer was an in-memory job and the flag that told it to run was not. The two are separate things now. The cover layer lives in memory and ends with the sheet that opened it; retention writes the colour as the app's own accent, which is the same colour drawn on your usual backgrounds rather than a repaint of everything. Turning the feature off hands back only what it wrote - a hue you picked yourself survives, even if a cover happened to be exactly that shade.
- A cover is shown as the colour it becomes: The seed read out of the cover art is whatever tone the artwork happens to be - a near-black navy, a blown-out cream - and the app painted that raw pixel as the Settings swatch and as the wash behind the detail hero. A dark poster produced an unidentifiable black chip in a dark app; a pale one flashed a full-strength light accent across the top of a dark sheet. Both ask for the accent the theme actually derives from the seed now, so the swatch is the colour the app is drawn with. Pure-black screens keep their black under the layer too: the elevation ramp's dim and bright surfaces were still taking the show's hue while everything around them was #000000.
- The Library's chips say what the editor says: The filter chips carried their own copy of the status labels and had drifted from the entry editor: a chip read "Paused" and "Planning" while the picker you had just used read "On-Hold" and "Plan to Watch", so a status you had set in one place was not findable under that name in another. Both now read one list of AniList's six statuses. The shared table fixes a quieter bug in the same place: the chips compared the raw status string, so an entry recorded under an older spelling - `ON_HOLD`, `WATCHING`, a `CLEARED` from the previous API - matched no chip at all and disappeared from every filter while still counting under "All".
- The skeleton sweep crosses the skeleton: The shimmer hung its highlight 300 pixels outside a fixed start-and-end range, so a narrow chip had the glow race through it in a tenth of the sweep while a tablet card never saw the far edge of it at all and looked permanently half-painted. The travel is measured off the box being drawn now, and every skeleton enters and leaves its own edges. It also now obeys the Instant motion setting like every other loop in the app does - the one control you have over motion had no idea the most constantly-drawn animation in the app existed - and it sweeps linearly, because the old ease-in-out braked into both edges, which read as the highlight stopping in the middle of a card and starting again.
- The wave stops restarting under your thumb: The wavy progress bar only built its travelling phase when the title had progress on it, so the first episode watched - or scrubbing back through a list - tore down the animation and rebuilt it at the exact moment you were interacting with the bar, and the wave jumped rather than carried on. Whether the loop is allowed to exist is now a question of visibility and motion style, and your thumb's position decides only whether the phase is read. Two related: a screenful of wave bars is a screenful of animations that kept ticking with the screen off, and every caller that sized the bar itself had its height overridden by the component's default - a 6dp row in a sequel card silently became 10dp.
- The bar drag was reading its own consumption: Holding the main bar and sliding your finger used to lift the bar and do nothing else: the pill stayed put and letting go opened whichever tab you had started on. The gesture marked each pointer move as consumed before asking how far it had moved, and a consumed change reports a delta of zero - so the accumulated travel was exactly zero for the whole drag, however far you went. The distance is read first now, and the bar follows your finger again.
- The feed stops rewinding its own cursor: Pulling the activity feed to refresh while it was already showing three pages re-read page one and left pages two and three on screen. The next scroll asked for page one again, because the thing that decides which page to fetch is the cursor and the refresh had set it backwards without removing the rows it covered. Only a page that actually arrived moves the cursor now; a refresh asks for one and a failed refresh asks for nothing.
- A signed-out session stops asking for a token: Every API request out to the network re-read the stored token, and with no token stored that fell through to a coroutine-blocking lookup - so an app left signed out paid a disk round trip on every single request, forever, on the thread that built the request. A signed-out session is remembered now and the lookup happens once.
- A cache write can no longer fail a fetch: Saving a snapshot of a screen to disk was part of the success path, so a full storage or a permission change turned a response AniList had already returned into an error screen. The write is best-effort now: the data is displayed and the copy for next time is simply missing. The serialize step is covered too, because a payload that cannot be written is not a reason to show nothing.
- Signing out forgets who you follow: Clearing the detail cache on sign-out left the friends list in memory, and the next session - a different account on the same phone - could be served the previous viewer's follower avatars before its own fetch landed. Per-viewer data is cleared with the rest now.
- The library stops spinning when it has nothing: When an overview refresh failed and the app fell back to the cached copy, the cached copy still said its library section was loading. The loader never stopped, because nothing else was going to write that flag again - the request it was waiting on had already returned an error. A failure that keeps the cache now marks the section as failed rather than as pending.
- One thread, one fetch, and counts that survive the sheet: Opening a comment thread cancelled the previous thread's work, but not a second open of the same thread, so two responses could arrive in either order and the older one won. Posting a reply or deleting one updated the feed's reply count only if the thread sheet was still composed - so closing it quickly, which is what reading a reply does, lost the count and the row went on saying three when it held four. Both updates happen before that check now.
- The social chip knows what it is showing: The followers / following switch dimmed the selected state while a list was loading or had failed, because the selected list is only readable from a successful state. Tapping Following and watching it load put the highlight back on Followers, which reads as the app having switched it back.
- The social tab stops spinning at a profile that hasn't answered: Opening the Social tab while the profile around it was still arriving left the followers switch on its skeleton with nothing coming: the fetch needs AniList's id, had none, and published a `Loading` whose only exit was the request it had just declined to make. It now says the profile hasn't finished loading and puts a retry under it, and the id that eventually lands starts the fetch from that failure. The same tab had a second way to hang - its re-entry trigger only fired from an idle state, so a visit after a cancelled or failed one never asked again. That is now a rule about which states are worth starting from, not about one state string.
- A refresh keeps the rows, and a failing half keeps the other: Refreshing the followers list replaced the faces already on screen with skeletons, so a refresh that found nothing new read as the account having emptied. The rows stay and a small spinner beside the chip says the same thing instead. The tab fetches both halves on one tap, and the half nobody had asked for failing used to swap the rows you could read for an error screen: the failure is a line under the list now, and only the header of the half that failed drops its count rather than claiming zero. A chip tap during a refresh of a list that had no rows yet was also dropped on the floor - it moves the selection now, without cancelling and re-issuing the download already in flight.
- Another person's profile can be read as a library: A follower, an account you follow, or a stranger reached by name gains a List tab that shows their list with their own status sections - the page every Social row was tapping toward with nowhere to arrive. Your own profile deliberately does not get it, because that list is the Library page on the main bar, and the borrowed one ignores the type, filter and sort you saved there: reading somebody else's things through your view of your own is not the same screen twice. The download the tab needs is asked for when the tab opens, so a profile visited for a banner and a bio no longer costs one request per 500 entries.
- A profile opened with nobody in it says so: The by-id route read its argument as `getInt("userId") ?: 0`, so a stripped or malformed link asked AniList for user zero and painted whichever account that is as a profile with a real name and a real bio - a routing bug wearing somebody else's face. A non-positive id with no name either is now a failure the reader can leave. A tap on a follower also carries that person's name along with their id: the bar reads the name instead of `Profile` for the length of a round trip, and two follower profiles no longer share a saved-state key that differed only by a number.
- A tab keeps its place: Profile tabs animate in and out, and the outgoing tab is destroyed rather than hidden - so the social tab's search text, its grid-or-list choice and its scroll position were lost on every round trip through Overview, and the comment composer reopened with whatever the last session had typed. Each tab now keeps its own saved state while it is off screen. The same pass made the reply box honest about being signed out: it was gated on demo mode, which is not the same thing.
- The calendar can look at one week: The activity heatmap showed a window of weeks and nothing else. A toggle reads the current week as rows of bars with the day names beside them, which answers the question the grid cannot: how much did I do today and on which days around it. The month header also stops drifting out of alignment with the grid it labels - each label was padded from a different edge than the cells under it.
- Replies sit under who they answer: A thread of replies was a flat list, so an argument between two people read as eight people talking to nobody. A reply that opens with a name is now indented under the most recent thing that person said - two levels, the same depth AniList's own site stops at - and the threading is computed once per thread rather than once per row, because the answer depends on everything above it.
- The update download gets a deadline and an honest bar: Three small things in the updater. A transfer that resumed from a partial file reported a total one byte short whenever the server did not declare a length, so the progress bar sat at 99 percent until the end. A server that keeps trickling bytes just inside the read timeout could hold an update in progress forever, and the dialog has no cancel button; the download now has an overall ceiling. And the check that a finished file is an APK asked for four bytes and accepted whatever the stream felt like returning, which is not always four.
- Thirty-six more ways it ended: The dark tone gains thirty-six lines - cancelled shows, studios that no longer exist, the wiki page with a section called Unresolved. The pool is above four hundred dark lines now, and the shuffle bag still shows each filtered line once before repeating any.
